beats.text: The wind turns, and with it comes the warm, grassy musk of a horse foal that has strayed from its herd.
You drop until your belly brushes the frost-stiff stems and edge forward, paw by paw. The foal tears at a tuft and flicks an ear at a fly.
You burst out of the grass. The foal is only starting to turn when your weight takes it down, and your sabers find its throat.
Afterwards you eat crouched low, ears turning at every sound. A kill out in the open soon draws other hunters.
The wind turns, and with it comes the warm, grassy musk of a horse foal that has strayed from its herd.
You creep closer until you can hear it chewing. Then a stem snaps under your hind paw.
The foal's head jerks up. It squeals and races back to the herd, and the mares are already turning to meet it.
You stand in the flattened grass with your heart pounding and your belly still empty.
You know this scent before you see who it is. {catName} is waiting on a flat stone where the path bends.

beats.text: {catName} is standing on a flat stone where the path bends, tail low and still.
{catName} smells of a wound that's still healing, and of other cats.

parts.beat: {catName} smells of a wound that's still healing, and of other cats.

beats.text: For a heartbeat neither of you moves.
{catName}'s lip lifts off the tip of a saber. Oh. You. I was hoping you'd gone somewhere else. What do you want?

parts.beat: {catName}'s lip lifts off the tip of a saber.

parts.say: Oh. You. I was hoping you'd gone somewhere else. What do you want?

beats.speaker: {catId}

parts.beat: {catName} doesn't bother getting up.

parts.say: Still alive, stray? Say what you want and be quick about it.
I've got a patrol soon. What do you want?
If you're not here to talk about big game, I'm not interested. Are you?

parts.beat: {catName} keeps an eye on the cubs tussling behind {him}.

parts.say: I'm watching the cubs. What do you want?
You're in my way. Is there something you need?

parts.beat: {catName} goes still, as if hoping you hadn't spotted {him}.

parts.say: You found me. I was listening to the grass. What is it?
I'm old and I'm tired, and I'm not looking for company. What do you want?
You're still in the Vale, then. I have the crag to see to. Are you stopping, or going on?

parts.beat: {catName} doesn't stop pacing.

parts.say: I'm in the middle of training. Are you staying, or do I carry on?

parts.beat: {catName} keeps {his} eyes on the slope.

parts.say: Quiet, there's elk on that slope. Are you staying or going?
Oh. You. I was hoping for a bit of time on my own. What is it?
You walked right across my hare tracks. Again. What do you want?

parts.beat: {catName} glances towards the dens.

parts.say: Keep your voice down, the cubs are asleep. What did you need?

parts.beat: {catName} steps across the path.

parts.say: You again. I'm on watch, so make it quick. What do you want?
I was going over the names, and now I've lost my place. What is it?
Back again. I don't need looking after, if that's why you're here. What is it?

parts.beat: {catName} looks past you down the trail, then back.

parts.say: Oh. It's you. I thought for a moment it was somebody else. What do you want?

parts.beat: {catName} turns the torn side of {his} face towards you.

parts.say: Look all you like. What do you want this time?
I'm not in the mood for talking. Is it important?
I was just heading off. What is it?

parts.beat: {catName} lifts {his} head slowly.

parts.say: I'm fine where I am. I don't need help. What brings you?

parts.beat: {catName} doesn't look up.

parts.say: You again. I said I don't want trouble. What do you want?

parts.beat: {catName} keeps {his} eyes on the water.

parts.say: I'm looking. Can it wait?
If you're not here with news of Mistwood, I don't have much to say. Do you have any?

parts.beat: {catName} speaks before you can.

parts.say: Quietly. I've got a lot to see to today. What brings you back?

parts.beat: {catName} keeps between you and the trees behind {him}.

parts.say: Stay there. My family's close. What do you want?
Don't ask about the leg. Was there something else?

parts.beat: {catName} steps across the trail so you can't go further.

parts.say: Not that way. What do you want?
You're standing on a trail I'm trying to keep clear. What is it?

parts.beat: {catName} is quiet today, ears low.

parts.say: Oh. Hello. Sorry, I'm not much company today. Did you want something?

parts.beat: {catName} sniffs the air in your direction.

parts.say: I know that scent. What is it you want, young cat?

beats.text: You again. I wondered if you'd still be around. {catName} glances back down the trail, then at you. Well? Are you stopping, or just passing?

parts.say: You again. I wondered if you'd still be around.

parts.beat: {catName} glances back down the trail, then at you.

parts.say: Well? Are you stopping, or just passing?

beats.speaker: {catId}

parts.say: You keep turning up on my field. That takes nerve, I'll give you that. Well, are you staying?

parts.beat: {catName} looks towards the river before looking at you.

parts.say: You've been down by the ford, haven't you? I can smell it. Are you stopping a while?
You're still catching hares, aren't you? I can tell. Come on, are you walking or not?
You're back. Not many strays come round again. Are you stopping, or just passing?

parts.beat: {catName} gives you a short nod.

parts.say: You again. You move quieter than most of our lot. Stopping, or passing?
Hello. I heard you coming a long way off. Are you staying, or just passing through?

parts.beat: {catName} settles {his} old bones onto the grass.

parts.say: You've come back. I didn't think you would. Are you sitting down, or moving on?

parts.beat: {catName} looks you over without hurrying.

parts.say: Back again. I've a little time before the evening hunt. Do you want to walk?
Oh, it's you. I thought you were somebody come to check on me again. Got time to walk?
You again. Still hunting on your own? Sit a while if you want, but keep low.

parts.beat: {catName} glances back at the caves before answering.

parts.say: You're not from the crag, so you won't ask me where I'm from. Want to walk a bit?

parts.beat: {catName} looks up from a line of prints in the snow.

parts.say: Hello. Don't step there, I'm reading these. Are you stopping, or just passing?
Hello again. The cubs finally settled, so I have a moment. Do you want to sit?
Back on our border? I'm on watch, but I can talk while I watch. Are you stopping?

parts.beat: {catName} squints, then nods.

parts.say: Ah, I remember your name. I don't let names slip. Will you sit with me?

parts.beat: {catName} eases up off the stone.

parts.say: Hello again. It's been quiet out here since you passed. Will you sit, or are you travelling?
You again. No, I'm not waiting for anybody. Well, not really. Do you want to sit?
You keep coming back. Maybe you're more useful than you look. Walking, or not?

parts.beat: {catName} checks behind you, the way {he} always does.

parts.say: Just you again? Good. Do you want to walk, or just say hello?

parts.beat: {catName} sniffs your shoulder.

parts.say: You've been somewhere new, I can smell it. Walk with me and tell me where?
Hello, dear. You came back. Will you sit down for a while?
You keep coming back, and I still don't know why. Are you staying?
Hello again. Have you seen any cubs by the water? Do you want to walk the bank with me?

parts.beat: {catName} sniffs you hopefully.

parts.say: No Mistwood scent on you? Oh well. Are you stopping a while?
You came back to the wood. I wasn't sure you would. Do you have time to walk?
You again. Keep away from the Mere side and we can talk. Are you stopping?

parts.beat: {catName} shifts {his} weight off {his} bad leg.

parts.say: Back again? I'm about to walk the long trail. Want to come, or just say hello?
You found me again. I'm still not telling you where the dens are. Stopping, or passing?

parts.beat: {catName} looks up from a row of old pawprints in the mud.

parts.say: Hello. I'm checking the marsh trail. Do you want to walk it with me?
Hello again! It's still so quiet in here. Will you stay a bit?
Ah, it's you. My eyes aren't good, but my nose is. Will you sit, or are you rushing off?

beats.text: {catName}'s ears shoot up. You came back! I mean, hello. Will you stay a while?

parts.beat: {catName}'s ears shoot up.

parts.say: You came back! I mean, hello. Will you stay a while?

beats.speaker: {catId}

parts.beat: {catName} gives you a slow, toothy look.

parts.say: The stray who doesn't run. Come on, walk the field with me and let them all see it.

parts.beat: {catName} trots over, then remembers to look tough.

parts.say: Hey. I mean, oh, it's you. Want to walk? Nobody's watching right now.

parts.beat: {catName} grins at you.

parts.say: There you are! I've been wanting to tell somebody about the herd on the plain. Walk with me?

parts.beat: {catName} comes over, still watching the cubs.

parts.say: Good, a grown cat to talk to. Will you stay a while? They can wrestle without me.
Oh good, it's you. I could use some company that doesn't shout. Will you walk with me?

parts.beat: {catName}'s ears turn towards you, bright and eager.

parts.say: You came back! Nobody else in the field ever wants to just talk. Will you stay?

parts.beat: {catName} looks honestly glad to see you.

parts.say: Come here, come here. The young ones don't listen to me any more. Will you sit and talk a while?

parts.beat: {catName} tips {his} head, almost pleased.

parts.say: I wondered when you'd come by again. Walk with me to the ridge and tell me how the Vale's treating you?

parts.beat: {catName} bounds down the rocks to you.

parts.say: You're back! Good, somebody to talk to who isn't watching me for mistakes. Walk with me?

parts.beat: {catName} shifts over to make room on the rock.

parts.say: Come and lie here. You can see the whole herd from this spot. Are you staying a while?

parts.beat: {catName}'s bobtail twitches up.

parts.say: It's you! You're the only cat round here who doesn't look at me like a puzzle. Will you stay?

parts.beat: {catName} waves you over with a flick of {his} ear.

parts.say: Come and look at these tracks with me. A hare went by not long ago. Are you staying?

parts.beat: {catName} comes to meet you, moving softly.

parts.say: I'm glad you came by. It's nice to talk to somebody who isn't chewing my tail. Will you stay a bit?

parts.beat: {catName} lets {his} guard drop, just a little.

parts.say: You came back. Most strays don't bother. Will you walk the border with me for a while?

parts.beat: {catName} pats the stone beside {him} with a paw.

parts.say: There you are. Will you sit and tell me your mother's name, if you know it? I like to keep everybody's.

parts.beat: {catName}'s old face creases with pleasure.

parts.say: You came back. Not many do, at my age. Sit with me a while?

parts.beat: {catName} jumps up.

parts.say: It's you! Good. I've been sitting here talking to myself. Will you stay a while?

parts.beat: {catName} falls in beside you like an old friend.

parts.say: There you are. Walk with me? I want to hear what you've seen near Bonefield.

parts.beat: {catName} looks pleased, then hides it badly.

parts.say: Oh, it's you. Fine, I'm glad. Will you walk with me a while?

parts.beat: {catName} bounds up the trail to you.

parts.say: You! I've found a new way round the gorge. Want to see it, or are you busy?

parts.beat: {catName}'s whole face lights up.

parts.say: Oh, it's you! Come and sit. I've been saving up things to tell you.

parts.beat: {catName} almost smiles.

parts.say: I didn't think anybody would come back after hearing about me. Sit down, if you want.

parts.beat: {catName} hurries up the bank to you.

parts.say: Oh, you came back! Walk the river with me? It's easier with somebody to talk to.

parts.beat: {catName}'s ears go right up.

parts.say: You came back! Have you been anywhere near the fog? Come on, walk with me and tell me.

parts.beat: {catName}'s tired face softens.

parts.say: I'm glad it's you. I could do with talking to somebody who doesn't need anything from me. Will you stay?

parts.beat: {catName} lets out a breath when {he} sees it's you.

parts.say: Oh, good, it's only you. Walk with me along the high ground? I don't go near the water.

parts.beat: {catName} limps over fast, grinning.

parts.say: You're back! Come on, walk with me. I promise I can keep up.

parts.beat: {catName} comes out of the fog with a small, wry look.

parts.say: Hello, you. I tracked you here, you know. Walk with me, as long as it's away from the dens?

parts.beat: {catName} brightens.

parts.say: Oh, good timing! Come and learn the safe way through the marsh. Will you walk with me?

parts.beat: {catName} hurries over, bobtail up.

parts.say: You came back! I was hoping you would. Will you stay and tell me where you've been?

parts.beat: {catName} turns {his} cloudy eyes towards you and smiles.

parts.say: Come and sit by me. I like a visitor who comes back. Will you stay a while?

beats.text: Oh, and I've heard a few things lately, if you ever want the news.

parts.say: Oh, and I've heard a few things lately, if you ever want the news.

beats.text: The Bonefield smells of old blood and trampled grass. You're crossing open ground beside a mammoth's ribs when the wind brings you a fresh cat scent, close by and not hiding.

parts.beat: The Bonefield smells of old blood and trampled grass. You're crossing open ground beside a mammoth's ribs when the wind brings you a fresh cat scent, close by and not hiding.

beats.text: {catName} rises out of the tall grass like the ground belongs to {him}, and under Bonefield law it does. {He} walks a slow circle round you.

parts.beat: {catName} rises out of the tall grass like the ground belongs to {him}, and under Bonefield law it does. {He} walks a slow circle round you.

beats.text: {catName} snorts and looks past you at the empty grass. On your own? Then nobody's going to drag you home if you get hurt out here.

parts.beat: {catName} snorts and looks past you at the empty grass.

parts.say: On your own? Then nobody's going to drag you home if you get hurt out here.

beats.speaker: {catId}

parts.beat: {catName} sniffs at you and frowns.

parts.say: You smell of the river. Don't hang around the ford, it's not worth the trouble.
Another hare-catcher, by the look of you. You wouldn't last long out here on the big game.

parts.beat: {catName} stands between you and the cubs' hollow.

parts.say: Keep away from our cubs. I won't ask nicely if you don't.
You walk loudly for a hunter. I'd go hungry, moving like that.

parts.beat: {catName} has been watching you for a while before {he} speaks.

parts.say: I heard you coming a long way off. The others will smell you soon enough.

parts.beat: {catName} looks at you with tired, old eyes.

parts.say: I've seen plenty of strays walk in here. Most of them were smarter about leaving.

beats.text: {catName} stops right in front of you. Our leader doesn't care where strays come from, only whether they run. So, are you going to run?

parts.beat: {catName} stops right in front of you.

npc_initiative.mistwood.request_help.v1.text: {catName} steps out of the marsh fog, muddy to the shoulders. “Our elders haven't eaten in days, and there aren't enough hunters left to feed them. Could you bring me a hare from these marshes, or anything small? I'll carry it to them myself.”

beats.text: Fog lies thick on the marsh. You're lying still in the reeds when you hear a paw pull out of the mud behind you.
{catName} steps out of the fog, muddy to the shoulders, and stops a little way off.
“Don't call out. I don't want anybody hearing us.”
“Quietly, please. Voices carry in this fog, and I don't want mine carried home.”
“Quietly, please! I know, I came to you. I just don't want the dens hearing us.”

“Our elders haven't eaten in days. We lost too many hunters when the ice broke, and there aren't enough of us left to feed everybody. Our leader would say a Mistwood cat doesn't beg from strangers. Well, I'm asking anyway.”
“Do you hunt on your own? Is it hard?”
“Could you bring me a hare from these marshes, or anything small? I'll carry it to them myself, and nobody needs to know where it came from.”

gossip.bonefieldBorder: “Bonefield's been pushing at the marsh edge. I keep finding their scent there, so I can't hunt the far reeds any more.”

replies.ask: “They'd say no, and then they'd keep an eye on me. Since the Breaking, everybody keeps an eye on everybody.”
replies.decline: “I understand. Forget you saw me out here. Please.”
replies.reminder: Did you find me a hare? Anything small from these marshes would do.
replies.kept: {catName} takes the meat gently, the way you'd carry a cub. “They'll eat tonight. Thank you.”
replies.broken: {catName} keeps a little distance. “So nothing's coming. All right. I'll manage.”
replies.keptShare: “This is for the elders, isn't it? You remembered. They'll eat tonight.”

beats.text: {catName} is standing in the middle of the path, far enough off that you can stop without crowding.

parts.beat: {catName} is standing in the middle of the path, far enough off that you can stop without crowding.

beats.text: That's close enough. On the crag we give our names before we come any nearer. What's yours?

parts.say: That's close enough. On the crag we give our names before we come any nearer. What's yours?

beats.speaker: {catId}

parts.beat: {catName} squares up, trying to look bigger.

parts.say: Stop there. I'm meant to ask your name before you come any closer. So what is it?
That's far enough, you'll spook the elk. What's your name?

parts.beat: {catName} hesitates, as if unsure how this part goes.

parts.say: Um, hello. On the crag we're supposed to give names before anything else. What's yours?

parts.beat: {catName} glances at the prints you've left in the snow.

parts.say: You've been walking through my hare tracks. Before you go any further, what's your name?
Softly, please, there are cubs asleep up there. Will you tell me your name?

parts.beat: {catName} doesn't move from the middle of the path.

parts.say: Stop there. Nobody comes nearer the caves without a name. What's yours?

parts.beat: {catName} leans forward, ears pricked.

parts.say: A new cat! Tell me your name, and say it clearly. I'll want to remember it properly.

beats.text: You're very loud, you know.

parts.say: You're very loud, you know.

beats.speaker: {catId}

beats.text: {catName} is standing by a tree, much closer than you'd thought.

parts.beat: {catName} is standing by a tree, much closer than you'd thought.

beats.speaker: {catId}

beats.text: Sound carries in the fog, and we've had enough trouble. Can you keep it down?

parts.say: Sound carries in the fog, and we've had enough trouble. Can you keep it down?

beats.speaker: {catId}

parts.beat: {catName} keeps {his} body between you and the trees behind.

parts.say: My family's close by, and noise carries in this fog. Will you keep your voice down?
You'll have every cat in the wood out here, stomping like that. Can you keep it down?

parts.beat: {catName} glances behind {him}, then back.

parts.say: Quieter. I don't want anybody following the noise to where we live. Will you keep it down?
Careful, that ground's soft and you're very loud. Can you keep it down?

parts.beat: {catName} sounds almost apologetic.

parts.say: Sorry, I have to ask. The others get upset when there's noise in the fog. Could you keep it down?

parts.beat: {catName} turns {his} cloudy eyes towards the sound of you.

parts.say: I heard you long before I smelled you, young cat. Can you keep it down for an old cat's sake?
